request.what: Fund Hydra v2 production hardening and performance improvements through four workstreams: performance optimization, operational excellence, ecosystem support, and developer experience/maintenance.

claims.claim: The proposal requests ₳5,100,781 for Hydra work that is described as milestone-gated with independent third-party assurance and Intersect administrative treasury governance.
Hydra is described as the only production-grade Layer 2 on Cardano and the only production-ready scaling solution that gives Cardano sub-second finality with L1-grade settlement guarantees.
The document says Hydra is already used or has powered Delta DeFi, Masumi, Hydra Doom, Glacier Drop, Intersect voting infrastructure, VTech Labs, Blockfrost, and Midgard.
The proposal claims Cardano L1 has over two hours of finality, approximately $0.17 per payment transaction, and roughly 7 to 10 TPS, making high-performance applications uncompetitive on L1.
The document claims a single Hydra Head can process up to 1,000+ TPS in payment benchmarks and that aggregate throughput scales close to linearly across independent Heads.
The proposal states that Hydra enables sub-second finality, near-zero or zero transaction costs inside a Head, high throughput, and settlement back to Cardano L1.

The proposal argues Hydra can attract and retain high-performance builders by making DeFi, AI agent micropayments, gaming, consumer payments, point of sale, and verifiable information processing viable on Cardano.

The document claims Hydra activity can support treasury sustainability because head lifecycle transactions create L1 fees and applications with non-zero internal fees can route a portion to the L1 treasury on settlement.

The proposal says upcoming L1 upgrades such as Leios and Peras will improve the base layer but cannot provide the zero-fee, sub-second, high-throughput envelope required by high-performance applications.

The proposal claims it advances treasury KPIs for TVL, monthly active users, monthly transactions, throughput capacity, reliability and uptime, and annual protocol revenue, and aligns with Pillars 1, 2, 4, and 5.

summary: The document requests ₳5,100,781 for milestone-gated Hydra v2 hardening and adoption work, asserting significant technical, adoption, and treasury benefits but providing mostly proposer-stated support in the supplied text rather than detailed budget, feasibility, alternatives, failure-mode, or impact analysis.
